title: Magento's nginx sample overrides php_admin_value, and that breaks the PHP2Shell memory_limit stopgap
summary:
PHP's main stopgap for the first PHP2Shell bug (CVE-2026-109618) is to remove the memory limit by setting memory_limit=-1, somewhere applications can't change it. The usual advice is php_admin_value in the FPM pool.
On a Magento store using the stock nginx config, that doesn't work. The value comes back as 756M, and ini_set() failing makes it look locked in.
The real fix is updating PHP. PHP's words: "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." The fixed releases are 8.
content:

To create a Google Play developer account, sign up on the Play Console sign-up page with a Google account, accept the Developer Distribution Agreement, pay the one-time US$25 registration fee, choose a personal or an organization account, and verify your identity. You must be at least 18.
Most of it takes an evening. The parts that take longer are identity verification, a D-U-N-S number if you register a business, and, for new personal accounts, the closed test before your first public release.
content:
To create a Google Play developer account, sign up on the Play Console sign-up page with a Google account, accept the Developer Distribution Agreement, pay the one-time US$25 registration fee, choose a personal or an organization account, and verify your identity. You must be at least 18.
Most of it takes an evening. The parts that take longer are identity verification, a D-U-N-S number if you register a business, and, for new personal accounts, the closed test before your first public release.
